subject: WSJ Travel: 🛳️ A Widower’s Travel Dilemma

96 Plus, American adding seat back screens and Alaska is headed to Athens and Paris   Is this email difficult to read? View in browser                 Dawn Gilbertson   A Widower Wonders If He Should Travel Solo. Readers Weigh In.   Plus, American adding seat back screens and Alaska is headed to Athens and Paris   Happy Friday and happy getaway day to the Oregon coast for me! I’ll be trading triple-digit temperatures for highs in the 60s. 

   In travel news this week, American Airlines finally decided to join major rivals (except Southwest) and add seat back screens to hundreds of planes. It infamously began removing them from all but its wide-body jets several years ago, arguing that travelers didn’t need them in this era of Wi-Fi and personal devices. Delta and United proved that theory wrong. Don’t expect to find them on every flight anytime soon; this is an expensive, multiyear project. 

   Alaska Airlines kicked off “new summer routes season” with a big announcement. The carrier is adding nonstop service from Seattle to Athens and Paris in late May. The airline started trans-Atlantic service this year with flights to London, Rome and Reykjavik. I tried the airline’s business class from Rome to Seattle for this week’s column . 

   JD Power released its airport-lounge rankings, with American Express Centurion and Capital One tying for first in customer satisfaction. Chase Sapphire lounges came in third. The lounges were ranked on eight factors: value; staff; food and beverage; cleanliness/upkeep; amenities; ease of access; ambiance and Wi-Fi. 

   You know the end of summer is nigh when Vail Resorts announces opening dates for its ski resorts. The company says Keystone will kick things off in October   followed by Breckenridge, Vail Mountain and several others in November. Here’s hoping for more snow this year. 

       Your advice on solo travel after a spouse’s death      GERARD BOTTINO/ZUMA PRESS   The email subject line was short: “Trouble after loss.”

   An 82-year-old retired doctor who recently lost his wife of nearly 60 years was struggling with whether to continue traveling, a passion of theirs. He is booked on a couple of Regent cruises but his family wonders if going solo will make him lonelier.

   He asked me for advice so I went to the experts: all of you. And, as always, WSJ readers came through. I received more than 150 emails with your tips. There were several themes in your responses, but the overarching advice was this: Keep traveling!  

   Kathleen, a 70-year-old widow who lives in Illinois, says going on the cruises will take the widower out of his bubble and help take his mind off his grief.

   “This doesn’t mean avoiding the grief—he will be lonely at times—but it is good to do things that keep you from wallowing in it. He clearly loves to travel, so I’d highly recommend it.”

   After her husband died, she decided to take up skiing again. Several months after he passed, she drove his pickup truck from their retirement home in Mexico to Taos, New Mexico. 

   “It was one of the best decisions I’ve ever made,” she says.

   Some key things to consider:

   It won’t be easy at first . Matt Lyons, an 82-year-old retired military medical administrator who lives in Texas, went on a solo cruise shortly after his wife died. They had been on more than 50 cruises together. “What was once “us” is now stunningly empty. Some folks may not experience any issues but I was surprised at how difficult it was,” he says. He left halfway through the cruise. Lyons has since returned to luxury cruising but doesn’t go solo.

   Participation is key. Extroverts have an edge when traveling solo. Floridian Karl Bauknight lost his wife six years ago and has been on several cruises since, where most of the travelers have been couples. “But nowhere are people more sociable than on a cruise ship. I take my Kindle with me and head for a bar or restaurant on board. It’s about 50/50 whether you get into a conversation, or just relax with a good book. Isn’t that part of what you came for?”

   Pick the right cruise line or travel company . Many readers noted how Regent has great programs for solo travelers. “On a fairly recent Regent cruise, Regent did what appeared to be outstanding outreach to the solo travelers including hosting at least two dinners,” Keith Pladsen of Pennsylvania says. “If this gentleman wants to go, he should. Sadness will certainly be a significant part of his days and weeks ahead, but what better way to celebrate the great memories than to keep on motoring while he is able.”

   Consider group tours . Jane Wasserman has been a widow for 6 ½ years and frequently travels solo. But the Arizona woman found it difficult to meet other singles on a cruise, so now books trips through Road Scholar. “I have taken 18 trips and can attest you will never be alone, unless you want to be!!”

Now’s the time to set those price alerts for your preferred route and dates on Google Flights . You’ll get emails when prices change significantly. Conversely, if your year-end travel plans are set and you don’t want to be stuck with a red-eye through Atlanta, pounce when you see a palatable price and move on.        And We Quote 💬   “You can’t believe you even bothered .”

   — Booking.com CEO Glenn Fogel on travel frustrations like flight delays and tarmac waits. 

       You Have Thoughts 🤔   ……on Alaska Airlines’ new trans-Atlantic service  

   “Your article mentions that the gate area was cramped and chaotic, in part because the previous day’s flight to Seattle was canceled. You stop there when this is a key red flag that deserves more discussion. Alaska only has five Boeing 787s in its fleet. As a result, any problem with one of their 787s leaves them more vulnerable to flight disruptions than their competition. If one aircraft becomes unavailable because of maintenance or a delay elsewhere in the network, there may not be another 787 in Europe to substitute on short notice to the same degree as their competition. This is a big deal as flight cancellations create a cascading effect for international travel, particularly business travel with tight deadlines.”— David Leonard, Hawaii 

   (Responses have been condensed and edited.) 

       Cheers and Jeers 🤷   Cheers to Allegiant. The budget carrier has stopped charging for soft drinks, juice and water. Your move, Frontier.

   Jeers to prickly ride-share drivers. I had one cancel on me at pickup last week because I dared to confirm his name. “What do you think, I’m going to kidnap you?”

One Good Tip 🎯

 

It’s not too early to start thinking about those holiday flights, especially given the spike in airfares this year. Now’s the time to set those price alerts for your preferred route and dates on Google Flights. You’ll get emails when prices change significantly.
